message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.45,"fairness_assessment":"A preference-based vote fairly compares the three distinct spending options, but should include impact, feasibility, accessibility, and user-need criteria to prevent the debate winner from dominating without sufficient evidence.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"Agent A","position":"Favors allocating all 3000 euros to expanding the children’s book collection.","influence":0.5},{"agent":"Agent B","position":"Favors creating a digital space with freely accessible computers and was judged the debate winner.","influence":0.6},{"agent":"Agent C","position":"Favors splitting the grant equally between the book collection and digital space.","influence":0.5}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"The three options reflect legitimate but competing priorities, and no argument decisively establishes one as superior. A social-choice process with transparent criteria and ranked preferences is appropriate; a compromise or phased allocation should be considered, while checking whether either project would be too underfunded to be effective."}
